newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast spot power firm amid clouds, showers.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast spot power firm amid clouds, showers.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. stayed firm Tuesday amid overcast skies and forecasted showers in parts of the region, market sources said.
"It's been a little warmer," said one regional utility trader. "No one is willing to commit to prescheduled (power) because of the possibility of rain."

In the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC), non-firm power for heavy-load hours on Wednesday delivered into northern portion of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) was assessed in the $14.75-$15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).
Electricity prices for non-firm, peak delivery at the Florida/Georgia interface were quoted at $21.00-$21.50.

Generation capacity in Florida increased as Florida Power & Light Co's 839 megawatt St. Lucie nuclear unit 1 on Hutchinson Island, Fla., achieved full output Tuesday. The unit were operating at reduced capacity for about two weeks to repair a leak in one of unit's transformers.
